result.topic_en: Euler observes that all resolutions of the series $\int\frac{1}{z^\mu}(\frac{1}{y^\nu})$ keep the exponent sum $\mu+\nu=m+n$ fixed, proposes classifying them into orders by this sum, and begins the first order ($m+n=2$).
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 151
10. In his formis notasse iuuabit, series formae, quam hic consideramus, $\int\frac{1}{z^{\mu}}(\frac{1}{y^{\nu}})$ non solum occurrere, sed etiam omnes ita esse comparatas, vt summa exponentium $\mu+\nu$ vbique sit eadem $=m+n$. Quo circa nostras inuestigationes ita in ordines distribui conueniet, vt omnes resolutiones, in quibus summa exponentium $m+n$ est eadem, ad eundem ordinem referantur: quandoquidem in iis eaedem series, quas hic euoluere constitui, occurrunt; atque si theorema in prima methodo erutum, quo est
$$\int\frac{1}{z^m}(\frac{1}{y^n})+\int\frac{1}{z^n}(\frac{1}{y^m})=\int\frac{1}{z^m}.\int\frac{1}{z^n}+\int\frac{1}{z^{m+n}}$$
in subsidium vocemus, hinc singulas series formae nostrae $\int\frac{1}{z^{\mu}}(\frac{1}{y^{\nu}})$ seorsim definire poterimus. Cum autem exponentes $m$ et $n$ vnitate minores esse nequeant, pro primo ordine erit $m+n=2$, pro secundo $m+n=3$, pro tertio $m+n=4$ et ita porro: cum autem sit $\int\frac{1}{z}$ infinita, pro seriebus quarum summa est finita hoc infinitum ex calculo egredi debet.
Ordo primus quo $m+n=2$.
11. Hic ergo vnico modo est $m=1$ et $n=1$; expressio $\int\frac{1}{z}.\int\frac{1}{z}-\int\frac{1}{z^2}$ in sequentem resoluitur:
$$\int\frac{1}{z}(\frac{1}{y})+\int\frac{1}{z}(\frac{1}{y})=2\int\frac{1}{z}(\frac{1}{y}).$$
Prior autem methodus dat
$$2\int\frac{1}{z}(\frac{1}{y})=\int\frac{1}{z}.\int\frac{1}{z}+\int\frac{1}{z^2}$$
quae

items.quote: Quo circa nostras inuestigationes ita in ordines distribui conueniet, vt omnes resolutiones, in quibus summa exponentium $m+n$ est eadem, ad eundem ordinem referantur
items.english: Therefore it will be convenient to distribute our investigations into orders, so that all resolutions in which the sum of exponents $m+n$ is the same are referred to the same order.

items.quote: hinc singulas series formae nostrae $\int\frac{1}{z^{\mu}}(\frac{1}{y^{\nu}})$ seorsim definire poterimus
items.english: hence we shall be able to determine each series of our form separately.

items.quote: cum autem sit $\int\frac{1}{z}$ infinita, pro seriebus quarum summa est finita hoc infinitum ex calculo egredi debet
items.english: but since $\int\frac{1}{z}$ is infinite, for series whose sum is finite this infinity must drop out of the calculation.
